newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ELECTRICITY PRICES END MIXED IN THIN TRADE.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ELECTRICITY PRICES END MIXED IN THIN TRADE.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished mixed in thin trade and easing physical power prices, industry sources said.

September Palo Verde (PV) closed up eight cents at $30.95 per megawatt hour (MWh) following exchanges in a range of $30.25-31.00, while October PV ended up 50 cents at $23.50 per MWh after exchanges at $23.10-23.70 per MWh.

September California Oregon Border (COB) settled down 14 cents at the $23.15 following exchanges at $22.55-23.20 per MWh, while October finished up 48 cents at $22.50 per MWh after trades at $22.20-22.75 per MWh.
NYMEX estimated volumes were not immediately available, but trade was said to be very light, with many industry players attending a Vancouver conference.
In the physical markets, firm, peak PV power for Friday was mostly sold at $53.00-57.00 a MWh, halved from yesterday's average, and traded in a wider range of $44.00-70.00, sources said.
Peak firm electricity at COB for Friday fell to $26.00-28.00 a MWh from Wednesday's $42.00-45.00 for delivery today.
In the six to 10 day forecasts, the West was expected to experience a cooling trend, moderating toward more seasonal summer temperatures.

In generation news, the 220 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Four Corners generating complex in New Mexico was expected to resume operation early Friday after being shut Wednesday to repair a boiler tube leak.
The plant's two 750 MW units (4 and 5) and two 185 MW units (1 and 2) were operating at full output, Arizona Public Service Co said.

Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Wednesday operating transmission capacity on the AC portion of the Pacific Intertie system will hold at 3,450 megawatt (MW), although the operating limit of the AC part of the system was increased to 3,800 MW.
Electricity output from the 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear power unit 3 in Wintersburg, Ariz., continued to hold at 90 percent power early Thursday for repairs to a condensate pump.
The adjacent 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear power unit 2 was also operating at 90 percent of capacity as of early Thursday as the unit coasts down to a scheduled refueling outage September 6.
